newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen up amid talk of higher Service bid.
newsitem.headline: Loewen up amid talk of higher Service bid.

text.p: Shares in Loewen Group Inc rose on Monday on anticipation that Service Corp International will announce a higher bid for Loewen of up to US$48 a share on Tuesday, analysts and traders said.

Loewen, North America's second biggest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries, last week rejected a US$43 a share bid from Service, the industry giant. Service's board meets on Tuesday to decide its next move.
Loewen rose 7/8 to 41-1/2 on Nasdaq, while Service fell 1/4 to 30-3/8. "Loewen is moving because everyone expects Service Corp to come back at a higher price," said a trader.
"There is talk of US$48 a share," he said.
Added another trader: "It will have to be north of US$46 to get people interested, say US$47 or US$48."

Analysts said the rise in Loewen stock also reflected such factors as company efforts to promote a US$350 million debt offering this week unrelated to its takeover defense, and Loewen's listing on Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange. Loewen announced over the weekend the acquisition of a Pennsylvania operator of 28 cemeteries and seven funeral homes, bringing its total acquisitions to US$100 million since the Service bid was announced on September 17.
In addition, sources said Service Corp retained Toronto-based TD Securities, which traders interpreted as a another sign that Service did not plan to back down.
They said TD had a niche in bridge financing and that its analyst who followed the funeral industry, Darren Martin, was well respected, they said.

Traders said Martin had talked about Loewen potentially being worth US$55 a share or more. This lead to speculation today that Service hired the firm partly "to keep him from writing any more stuff along those lines," said one trader. Martin was unavailable for comment.
